name: Touché Amoré
label: Deathwish
lede: A Los Angeles band fronted by a former Thursday fan-site kid, an eighteen-minute debut, and a record that turned Jeremy Bolm's mother's death into its most popular album.

eras.title: A Thursday fan site, a 7", and a festival that paid off
eras.text: Jeremy Bolm started Touché Amoré in Los Angeles in 2007 and built it the way a kid from the message boards would: tour by tour, on gas money. By the end of 2009 there was a 7" on No Sleep, a debut album that lasts eighteen minutes, and a festival slot that Bolm says told him the work was paying off.

years.h: Jeremy Bolm starts Touché Amoré in Los Angeles
years.p: [[Jeremy Bolm|c3401f13-df8b-45f6-bd20-6f91f67d2cd4]] forms the band in Los Angeles in 2007; it grows into a stable five-piece with guitarists [[Nick Steinhardt|fa1c73fc-8f3c-492c-8a26-7f974e093ae4]] and [[Clayton Stevens|3be4621b-8c12-4c8c-8617-853d18e1d1e4]] and drummer [[Elliot Babin|275829e0-2d23-4ddd-bb12-087e44481f46]].
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the formation to 2007 and places the band's first West Coast tours before the 2008 demo. It does not say who played bass at the start; [[Tyler Kirby|4d8b1b40-f69e-4bf3-a8fb-47ad3e671e45]] is listed as the bassist by 2010.

Bolm had a fan's route into music: he told Anti-Matter he first got noticed running an unofficial website for [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]]. Two years later Thursday's Geoff Rickly sings on the band's debut.

years.h: Debut 7" demo comes out on No Sleep Records
years.p: The self-titled 2008 demo 7" on No Sleep is the band's first release, after early tours of the West Coast. Two of its songs, "Broken Records" and "Honest Sleep", get re-recorded for the debut album.
years.xp: The 7" also puts Touché Amoré in the orbit of the label that would later release their split with [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]].

years.h: ...To the Beat of a Dead Horse: 11 songs in 18 minutes
years.p: The debut LP on 6131 Records, with Thursday's Geoff Rickly guesting on "History Reshits Itself" and Jeff Eaton of Modern Life Is War on "Always Running, Never Looking Back". Steinhardt designed the artwork.
years.xp:
Sources disagree on the date: Wikipedia's band page says June 2009 (through 6131 and Rickly's Collect Records), the album page says August 4, 2009 (6131). Nick Steinhardt also plays bass on the record.

Rock Sound gave it 9/10, and it landed on several best-of-2009 lists.
play: ...To the Beat of a Dead Horse

years.h: Sound and Fury 2009: the festival where the work paid off
years.p: Bolm names the 2009 Sound and Fury festival as the turning point, the moment his hard work started to pay off. It comes in the year of the debut album.
years.xp: Bolm told Alternative Press that early support tours paid about 150 bucks a night, so the band lived on merch sales and enough gas money to keep going.

eras.title: The wave, and a leak on purpose
eras.text: With the lineup set, Touché Amoré joined a run of splits and tours with La Dispute, Pianos Become the Teeth and Make Do and Mend. They leaked their own second album to build a crowd, then signed to Deathwish Inc. and made Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me in five days in Kansas.

years.h: Tyler Kirby on bass completes the lineup
years.p: By 2010 the band is Jeremy Bolm, Nick Steinhardt, Clayton Stevens, Elliot Babin and bassist [[Tyler Kirby|4d8b1b40-f69e-4bf3-a8fb-47ad3e671e45]], and it has not changed since.
years.xp: Alternative Press notes the same five-piece has held since 2010 and that Bolm compares it to a marriage. Wikipedia does not give Kirby's exact joining date or say who played bass before him.

years.h: Split with [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]] on No Sleep Records
years.p: Touché Amoré and the Michigan band swap songs on the split Searching for a Pulse/The Worth of the World, the start of a long touring partnership.
years.xp: A 2010 split with [[Make Do and Mend|0270a7d9-848a-41bc-99c0-cd396c970c55]] on 6131 and Panic follows the same year. La Dispute would take them to Europe in 2011.

years.h: Touché Amoré leak their own album to build a crowd
years.p: The band deliberately leaks Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me before it is out, so audiences already know the songs when they tour.
years.xp: Alternative Press describes it as a strategy: fans arrive knowing the words, and support slots turn into a breakthrough into the emo and hardcore revival crowd around [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]] and Balance and Composure.

years.h: Five days in Eudora, Kansas with producer Ed Rose
years.p: The band records Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me live at Black Lodge Recording in five days, aiming for a raw sound.
years.xp: Ed Rose produced, engineered and mixed; Carl Saff mastered.

years.cap: Cover of Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me
years.h: Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me arrives on Deathwish
years.p: The second LP is the first on Jacob Bannon's Deathwish Inc. and gets a Metacritic score of 81 and a 9/10 from Rock Sound. Before release the band reveals one piece of the artwork a week on Steinhardt's blog.
years.xp: "Amends", "Home Away from Here" and "~" streamed early. Rock Sound ranked the album No. 6 of 2011.
play: Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me

years.h: Europe with La Dispute, July 27 to August 12
years.p: Touché Amoré support [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]] across Europe from July 27 to August 12, 2011, their first big overseas run behind the new record.

years.h: Bolm launches Secret Voice as a Deathwish imprint
years.p: Jeremy Bolm starts the record label Secret Voice as an imprint of [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s Deathwish Inc. in 2012. The name comes from what he calls his low speaking register.

years.h: Live on BBC Radio 1: four songs with Jordan Dreyer
years.p: Recorded while touring with La Dispute, the EP has Jordan Dreyer of La Dispute guesting; Bolm says recording where the Smiths and Joy Division had played was meaningful.
years.xp: Released on Deathwish (DWI136), engineered by Simon Askew for BBC host Mike Davies. Songs: "~", "Home Away from Here", "I'll Deserve Just That" and "Amends". Wikipedia dates the release August 14, 2012; the band page says the session was recorded in May.

years.h: A European tour with Converge
years.p: Touché Amoré tour Europe with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] in November and December 2012, on the bill with the band of Deathwish founder Jacob Bannon.

eras.title: Turning thirty, panic, and Brad Wood
eras.text: With Brad Wood in the booth, Is Survived By turned the band's short, fast songs toward the anxiety of turning 30. The tours got bigger, and the band ended up at Coachella.

years.h: Is Survived By: 29 minutes, produced by Brad Wood
years.p: Recorded at Seagrass Studio in Los Angeles with [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]], it is the band's third album on Deathwish and its best-reviewed so far, at 87 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
Alternative Press's Scott Heisel called the breakdowns psychological rather than musical. Jon Simmons of Balance and Composure and Julia Blake of Vow guest. "Just Exist" came out July 30; the tracklist and artwork came July 17.

Alternative Press says the record deals with turning 30 and panic attacks.

years.h: Split with Title Fight and split with Pianos Become the Teeth
years.p: In 2013 the band releases a split with [[Title Fight|1154d345-8061-4d04-a52a-6214288523ac]] on Sea Legs and another with [[Pianos Become the Teeth|7436d471-fdce-42e8-a3cf-c0dc542c8524]] on Deathwish and Topshelf.

years.h: First tour of Russia, plus Reading, Leeds and Pukkelpop
years.p: The summer of 2014 takes Touché Amoré to Reading and Leeds in the UK, Pukkelpop in Belgium and, in August, Russia for the first time.
years.xp: Earlier that year they played SXSW, toured Europe with Birds in Row, and supported AFI in the US. Wikipedia says Bolm's mother died of cancer in 2014.

years.h: A Los Angeles hardcore band plays Coachella
years.p: Touché Amoré play Coachella in 2015, a milestone Alternative Press cites for the band's rise.
years.xp: The same year they toured Australia with Every Time I Die and released Self Love, a split 7" on Deathwish with Self Defense Family, with songs written and recorded together and produced by Will Yip.

eras.title: Stage Four
eras.text: Jeremy Bolm wrote about his mother's death from cancer, and the band left Deathwish for Epitaph Records to release it. It became their most popular record.

years.h: Touché Amoré sign to Epitaph for Stage Four
years.p: Exclaim reports the band signs to Epitaph Records for their fourth album, Stage Four.

years.big: Stage Four: his mother, and nothing else to write about
q: I couldn't write about anything else.
years.h: Stage Four: an album about Jeremy Bolm's mother
years.p: The fourth album, produced by [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]], is about the death of Bolm's mother from cancer; the title also counts the fourth record. [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] sings on "Skyscraper".
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Zoe Camp compared it to Sufjan Stevens's Carrie & Lowell; Metacritic has it at 84. Bolm told Anti-Matter it became the band's most popular record.

Wikipedia's band page dates the release September 16, 2016; its album page says September 24.

years.h: 10 Years / 1000 Shows: a live album at LA's Regent Theater
years.p: The band marks a decade and a thousand shows with a live record from the Regent Theater, released on Deathwish as a double LP.

years.h: Dead Horse X: the debut album re-recorded
years.p: For the tenth anniversary of ...To the Beat of a Dead Horse, the band re-records the whole album as Dead Horse X.
years.xp: Bolm told Anti-Matter he swapped a Morrissey reference for a nod to Leonard Cohen once Morrissey's public statements disappointed him.

years.h: "Deflector" is produced by Ross Robinson
years.p: The single "Deflector", released September 10, 2019, is the first sign of a partnership with producer [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]].

eras.title: Ross Robinson and the bigger sound
eras.text: Ross Robinson produced the last two albums, with guests from Andy Hull to Julien Baker and Lou Barlow, and Bolm says the sessions felt like therapy.

years.h: Lament: Ross Robinson, a flexi disc and Andy Hull
years.p: Recorded at The Bunker in Brooklyn with [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]], the album's only feature is [[Andy Hull|528476d9-1325-483d-ae1c-faf31511b4ec]] on "Limelight"; [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] sings backing vocals on "Reminders".
years.xp: Fans got "Limelight" on a flexi disc mailed in late July 2020. Bolm said he didn't want to write more about grief. Lament made #8 on Stereogum's best albums of 2020, and the "Reminders" video features friends with their pets, including Skrillex and Frank Iero.

years.h: "Nobody's" debuts live at Outbreak Fest in Manchester
years.p: Touché Amoré play their new song "Nobody's" at Outbreak Fest, Manchester, in 2024, months before its July 24 release.

years.cap: Cover of Spiral in a Straight Line
years.h: Spiral in a Straight Line on Rise Records, with Lou Barlow
years.p: The sixth album, made with [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]] at The Peaky Barnacle in Los Angeles, features [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] and Lou Barlow, and is their first on Rise Records.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Ellie Kovach praised the hooks; Kerrang! was mixed. Bolm told Anti-Matter the sessions were the closest thing to therapy he has had.

years.h: Touché Amoré headline Riot Fest in Chicago
years.p: The band announced in April that it would play Riot Fest in September 2025; the year also brings Live on BBC Radio 1: Vol 4 and Vol 5 on Rise.

sources.title: Anti-Matter: In conversation with Jeremy Bolm
